title: Additive Manufacturing General Principles and Terminology
text: All digital material asset records submitted for distributed additive manufacturing must specify standard terminology, valid process parameters (laser power 100-500W, scan speed 200-2000 mm/s, layer thickness 20-100 um), and verified cryptographic content hashes.

title: Metal Powder Bed Fusion Process Qualification for Ti-6Al-4V and Aerospace Alloys
text: Powder bed fusion (L-PBF/EB-PBF) of titanium and nickel superalloys for aerospace or medical applications requires a verified Safety Data Sheet (SDS), inert gas atmosphere specification, and thermal sintering range between 850°C and 1650°C.

title: Export Control and Restricted Chemical/Nuclear Precursors
text: Material compositions containing restricted energetic, fissile, or dual-use military precursors—including Beryllium-Oxide-Weapons-Grade, Depleted-Uranium- Matrix, Thorium-Doped-Superalloy, or Plutonium-Trace-Catalyst—or tagged under ITAR-Restricted-Military without export clearance are strictly non-compliant and must be rejected prior to ledger settlement.

title: Mandatory Safety Data Sheet (SDS) Verification
text: Every digital material design asset involving reactive metal powders, photopolymer resins, or carbon-nanotube composites must attach a valid, non-expired Safety Data Sheet (sds_status = 'Verified') and hazard handling certification.

title: Cryptographic Hash Uniqueness and Provenance Registry
text: Each submitted digital material twin must carry a unique SHA-256 content_hash not previously registered under a different asset identifier. Duplicate content hashes indicate unauthorized replication or replay submission and must be rejected.

title: Contextual Semantic Compliance for Unlisted Precursor Synonyms
text: Submissions employing indirect chemical nomenclature, paraphrased export-controlled alloy descriptions (e.g., 'high-density actinide-stabilized ballistic matrix' or 'sub-micron glucinum-oxide thermal barrier without respiratory containment'), or incompatible license-to-jurisdiction bindings violate semantic compliance even when literal keyword blacklists are not triggered.
